An interactive map of the island, county by county. Click any of the highlighted counties to read about a hike I've done there. The non-highlighted counties are inactive: they're either places I haven't yet hiked or places where the trip is still on the to-do list.

```{=html}
<div class="ie-map-wrapper">
  <div class="ie-map-stage">
    <svg id="ie-map" viewBox="0 0 800 900" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Map of the counties of Ireland with highlighted hikes"></svg>
    <div id="ie-tooltip" class="ie-tooltip" aria-hidden="true"></div>
  </div>
  <aside class="ie-legend" aria-label="Legend">
    <div class="ie-legend__item"><span class="ie-swatch ie-swatch--clickable"></span><span>Counties with documented hikes (clickable)</span></div>
    <div class="ie-legend__item"><span class="ie-swatch ie-swatch--inactive"></span><span>Other counties</span></div>
    <div class="ie-legend__counties">
      <strong>Documented:</strong>
      <a href="/ireland/wicklow.html">Wicklow</a> ·
      <a href="/ireland/donegal.html">Donegal</a> ·
      <a href="/ireland/sligo.html">Sligo</a> ·
      <a href="/ireland/mayo.html">Mayo</a> ·
      <a href="/ireland/down.html">Down</a>
    </div>
  </aside>
</div>

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/d3@7"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  const HIKES = {
    "Wicklow County": "/ireland/wicklow.html",
    "Donegal County": "/ireland/donegal.html",
    "Sligo County":   "/ireland/sligo.html",
    "Mayo County":    "/ireland/mayo.html",
  };

  const svg = d3.select("#ie-map");
  const tooltip = document.getElementById("ie-tooltip");

  d3.json("/assets/ireland-counties.geojson").then(function (geojson) {
    if (!geojson || !geojson.features) {
      console.error("Ireland GeoJSON failed to load");
      return;
    }

    const width = 800;
    const height = 900;

    const projection = d3.geoMercator().fitSize([width, height], geojson);
    const path = d3.geoPath().projection(projection);

    svg.selectAll("path")
      .data(geojson.features)
      .enter()
      .append("path")
      .attr("d", path)
      .attr("class", function (d) {
        const name = d.properties.name;
        return HIKES[name] ? "ie-county ie-county--clickable" : "ie-county";
      })
      .attr("data-name", function (d) { return d.properties.name; })
      .on("mouseenter", function (event, d) {
        const name = d.properties.name;
        tooltip.textContent = HIKES[name]
          ? name.replace(" County", "") + " — click to read"
          : name.replace(" County", "");
        tooltip.style.opacity = "1";
        tooltip.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "false");
      })
      .on("mousemove", function (event) {
        const stage = document.querySelector(".ie-map-stage").getBoundingClientRect();
        tooltip.style.left = (event.clientX - stage.left + 14) + "px";
        tooltip.style.top  = (event.clientY - stage.top + 14) + "px";
      })
      .on("mouseleave", function () {
        tooltip.style.opacity = "0";
        tooltip.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");
      })
      .on("click", function (event, d) {
        const url = HIKES[d.properties.name];
        if (url) {
          window.location.href = url;
        }
      });
  }).catch(function (err) {
    console.error("Failed to load Ireland GeoJSON", err);
    svg.append("text")
      .attr("x", 400).attr("y", 450)
      .attr("text-anchor", "middle")
      .attr("fill", "#c8102e")
      .attr("font-size", "14")
      .text("Map data could not be loaded.");
  });
})();
</script>
```

## How this map works

This is the page closest to my BAA1028 Workflow & Data Management module's principles in spirit. The map is rendered by JavaScript at page load time. The county boundary data lives in `assets/ireland-counties.geojson` as a separate structured data file rather than being baked into the page. The clickable counties are defined declaratively in a JavaScript object at the top of the script, so adding a new hike is a one-line change plus a new sub-page. The same separation of structured data from presentation that the rest of the portfolio uses (project frontmatter, repo statistics CSVs, languages chart) applies here.

The county boundary GeoJSON is sourced from the public-domain [click_that_hood](https://github.com/codeforgermany/click_that_hood) project by Code for Germany.
